problem: Image-based RL navigation policies (RGB/depth) fail under robot-to-robot changes (camera intrinsics/extrinsics) and hence sim-to-real, because prior sim-to-real work only matches textures/lighting and ignores the geometric meaning of observations. RL policies also suffer from partial observability.
motivation: Training RL on real robots is slow and dangerous, so policies must be trained in simulation and transferred without fine-tuning. Depth images still depend on camera parameters, so a robot-independent observation space is needed, and point clouds can also accumulate past observations to reduce partial observability.
key_idea: Convert depth/RGBD into point clouds projected into a fixed robot frame (a canonical, camera-independent observation space), integrate past frames by registration, and train a PointNet/ShellNet-based PPO policy with domain randomization.
insight: The ablation shows the canonical space matters: when camera parameters change at evaluation (Condition A), the RGBD baseline collapses to SR 0.10 while the point-cloud agent stays at 0.85, versus 0.87 for both under basic evaluation. Neither representation is robust to action-noise changes (Condition B), so domain randomization is still needed for the action space. PointNet and ShellNet perform almost identically on PointGoal with 1024 points.
method: Canonical projection: depth/RGBD points are transformed with camera intrinsics/extrinsics and the kinematic chain into a fixed robot frame (x,y,z), so they are agnostic of camera placement and FOV.
Frame integration: point clouds from previous steps are registered to the current one (GT poses in simulation, ICP-like; ORB-SLAM2 keyframes on the real robot) to address partial observability.
Downsampling: crop to a 10 m square around the robot, voxel-sample, then randomly sample to 1024 points (also acts like dropout); only depth/geometry is used.

Point cloud encoders: PointNet (shared FC layers + global pooling) and a modified ShellNet with added point-location encoding and multi-scale feature concatenation (Inception-style), replacing the Habitat CNN encoder; GRU/RNN + PPO actor-critic as in Habitat.
Domain randomization: camera intrinsics/extrinsics randomized per episode and a noisy base motion model; discrete motion primitives (forward, left, right, stop).
Safety-aware training: episodes end upon collision (reward* variant) and the footprint radius is set to 0.25 m instead of Habitat's 0.1 m.

setting.backbone: PointNet / modified ShellNet encoder + RNN + PPO actor-critic (trained from scratch); RGBD CNN baseline
setting.training_data: RL in Habitat on MP3D (or Gibson for sim-to-sim), 100K updates x 6 workers x 128 rollout = 76.8M steps; no extra data
setting.observation: Depth/RGBD converted to accumulated point clouds in robot frame (1024 points) plus point goal
setting.action_space: discrete: move forward, turn left, turn right, stop
setting.simulator: Habitat (MP3D, Gibson); real Toyota HSR robot
setting.privileged: GT poses used for point-cloud registration during simulation training/evaluation; real robot uses ORB-SLAM2 instead

numbers.extra: Camera and action-noise randomization in train and eval; collision ends episode; footprint 0.25 m; mean of 5 runs

numbers.method: PointNet, eval condition A (camera parameters changed)
numbers.extra: Unseen camera parameters at evaluation; trained with domain randomization

numbers.method: PointNet trained on Gibson, eval Gibson

numbers_note: Split names are inferred (the paper says evaluation sets of MP3D/Gibson); benchmark labels MP3D/Gibson-PointNav are approximate. Real-world result is only stated in text: about 75% of tasks solved, with no SPL. Table 1 and Table 4 also report non-randomized/basic evaluations and RGBD baselines, which are not included here.
results: Under robot randomization on MP3D, PointNet reaches SR 0.82 and SPL 0.68 versus the RGBD baseline's 0.54 and 0.44. With changed camera parameters the RGBD baseline drops to SR 0.10 while PointNet keeps 0.85. On the real HSR robot, the agent solves about 75% of tasks out of the box, while the RGBD baseline fails on non-trivial cases.
limitations: Requires an external point-cloud registration/SLAM system, which limits performance; GT poses are used in simulation.
Point-cloud networks are limited to about 1024 points because of memory and compute (ShellNet needs 35GB and about 2 weeks of training).

Robustness to action-space changes remains weak, and failures are mostly collisions with objects never seen. Real-world evaluation is limited to a single robot, with only a success percentage reported.
compares_to: Habitat RGBD PPO baseline (Savva et al. 2019)
